title: Unearned Days While the Company Stays Certified: Named Non-Owner Policy Requested Cancellations
content:
**Rule.** On a Named Non-Owner Policy term cancelled at the named insured's request, the unearned days shorten while the company stays certified to the state. The unearned days so set are the days used in figuring the unearned premium and the days the return entry carries.

**Operator certificate on file.** The named insured's Operator certificate on file is the SR-22 Operator Certificate or FR-44 Operator Certificate filing of the named insured whose status is filed, the FR-44 one when both are filed and the one recorded first when two of a form are filed; a certificate whose SR-26 has been sent has the status cancellation filed and is not on file; Owner and Owner-Operator certificates are not Operator certificates, and the term's own record of the certificate it was written to back is not read. These filings are the named insured's records with the Financial Responsibility Filings (SR-22 / FR-44) product.

**Count of unearned days.**
1. When the named insured has an Operator certificate on file, the unearned days — from the cancellation effective date, counted, to the expiration date, not counted — are reduced by the Financial Responsibility Filings (SR-22 / FR-44) product's SR-26 transmission days plus its certificate run-off days for that certificate.
2. When the named insured's Operator certificate has had its SR-26 sent (status cancellation filed, the FR-44 one when both forms have), the unearned days run from the later of the cancellation effective date and that certificate's end date to the expiration date.
3. With neither, the unearned days stand: from the cancellation effective date, counted, to the expiration date, not counted.

In every case the unearned days are never fewer than zero.

| Records show | Unearned days |
|---|---|
| a filed Operator certificate | days to expiration less the transmission days and run-off days for that certificate |
| an Operator certificate with SR-26 sent, end date after the cancellation effective date | days from the end date to expiration |
| an Operator certificate with SR-26 sent, end date on or before the cancellation effective date | days from the cancellation effective date to expiration |
| neither | days from the cancellation effective date to expiration |

*Abstract cases:* with 40 days to expiration and a filed certificate whose transmission and run-off days total S, the count is 40 less S; when S exceeds 40 the count is zero. With an SR-26 already sent and an end date 6 days after the cancellation effective date, the count is 34.
